Formulation  
An elderly male with known vascular risk factors (type 2 diabetes, hypertension, family history of heart disease) presents acutely with left-sided arm paralysis, facial tingling, speech difficulties, and dysphagia. These focal neurological signs are strongly suggestive of an acute cerebrovascular event (stroke). Living alone without immediate social support may increase vulnerability. Prompt emergency response is appropriate to reduce morbidity and mortality. No documented prior mental health issues at this time.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Acute neurological symptoms consistent with possible stroke  
- Patient Goal(s): Access emergency medical care promptly  
- Clinical Goal(s): Rapid assessment and treatment of suspected stroke to prevent further neurological damage  
- Actions (Patient): Remain at home, keep front door unlocked, sit in hallway for ambulance access, follow ambulance and hospital instructions  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Emergency ambulance called, stay on line to monitor patient until ambulance arrives, provide reassurance, inform hospital of suspected stroke  

Secondary Problem: Not recorded  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Recognition of stroke symptoms, importance of emergency treatment, instruction to keep door unlocked and await ambulance
